styles.name: Japandi
styles.description: warm earthy neutrals, light birch and oak, low slim-legged handcrafted furniture, linen and paper, a few well-chosen pieces and calm surfaces, handmade ceramics with gentle imperfection
styles.avoid: loud colours, many small objects, busy patterns

styles.name: Scandi
styles.description: bright white walls and pale wood, soft wool and sheepskin textiles, simple functional furniture, calm, cheerful and cosy

styles.name: Playful Montessori
styles.description: everything at child height: a low floor bed about 10 to 15 cm high, an open shelf no deeper than 40 cm with few toys and picture books facing front, art hung at child eye level, natural wood, wool and cotton, calm colours
styles.avoid: tall furniture, overfilled shelves, flashing plastic toys

styles.name: Retro Kids
styles.description: nostalgic childhood of the 70s to the 2000s: vintage wooden toys, handmade patterns, a vintage furniture piece, warm caramel and mustard accents

styles.name: Biophilic Nursery
styles.description: nature indoors: botanical touches, linen, a bouclé cushion, curved shapes such as an oval rug, a round shelf and wavy edges, soft greens and natural wood

styles.name: Playful Curves
styles.description: rounded arches, scalloped edges and soft curved furniture in gentle pastel colour pops on a calm cream base, clean Scandinavian craftsmanship

styles.name: Fun Haus
styles.description: circus-inspired playfulness: striped upholstery (caramel-and-cream or blue-and-cream) on the bed and cushions, sculptural arch- and pill-shaped cream furniture fronts, wavy edges, vintage circus art in small frames, one saturated blue accent; the loud pattern is balanced by a restrained blue, cream, caramel and brick palette, and stripes never appear on the wall behind the wallpaper
styles.avoid: stripes or dots on the wallpaper wall, loud busy curtains next to the mural, hanging balloons or lamps in front of the mural

styles.name: Boho
styles.description: warm relaxed layering in beige, terracotta, warm brown and muted green, cotton and textured textiles, natural wood

styles.name: Woodland Nature
styles.description: calm forest feeling: green, brown, beige and cream, solid wood and natural textiles, soft botanical touches, no literal animal decor

styles.name: IKEA Kids
styles.description: classic Swedish family-home look: light solid pine and white painted wood, a low pine children's table and stool (FLISAT style), a low white bed (KRITTER style), a low white-and-pine toy storage unit with pastel boxes (TROFAST style), simple cotton bedding, calm pastel accents on a white and wood base
styles.avoid: wardrobes, loft and bunk beds, tall units, a table with chairs, logos, brand labels or any readable text on furniture, glossy plastic toys

rules: Out in 2026: full themed rooms, loud wall colours, plastic decor, symmetric picture-frame grids; in: gender-neutral rooms, natural materials, layered warm light, furniture that grows with the child (Kindersein 26.03.2026)
One wall may be loud, the rest quiet; no pattern on other surfaces next to a patterned wall (allergutendinge 22.04.2026, wohnprofiblog 11.08.2026)
Warm oak looks cosier than white furniture and hides scratches; kids like more colour than adults expect (wohnlieberaumgefuehl 27.05.2026)

Competitor reference (kids-furniture studio, Instagram post of 26.10.2026): a striped corner daybed with a wavy headboard, sculptural cream fronts, vintage circus frames and a blue-cream-caramel-brick palette show what Fun Haus looks like in a real room; the striped wall itself only suits a listing whose wallpaper IS the stripe

realism.photo: A real editorial interior photograph for a German home magazine: natural window light with soft directional falloff and realistic contact shadows, true-to-life tactile materials (natural open-pore wood grain, woven linen fibers, organic textile texture with subtle signs of daily use), natural colour and authentic optical micro-contrast.
realism.note: Positive wording on purpose: Google's image guide says describe what you want, not what you don't; OpenAI's says ask for a real photograph and name materials and light. Camera body, lens and aperture are cues for the look, not a simulation.

staging.text: STAGING (the mural is the hero): a furnished, lived-in children's room of about 4.5 by 3.5 metres under a 2.8 m ceiling. The hero piece stands along a side wall with at most two small accessories beside it, and the child's own toys lie on the single floor rug. Everything near the mural wall is lower than 90 cm, so the drawing of the mural stays open and clear.
staging.brief: Only the items named in this scene are in the room, and the walls carry only the pictures named here.
staging.framingTall: a floor-to-ceiling section of the mural wall around the main motif of the mural, with the ceiling line at the top of the frame and the skirting board and a strip of floor at the bottom; the mural continues beyond the frame edges at its true scale
staging.note: Applies to every prompt the builder makes (the product is a wall mural). Owner 10.11: a furnished room; it replaces the 'almost empty room' rule of 06.11, which made every frame the same empty box. What stays from the owner's complaints: too many things hide the mural, a blanket lying about and a basket are junk. A tall frame (tallRatios) shows a SECTION of the wall floor to ceiling (framingTall), because a wide mural shown whole in a tall frame is squeezed and half the frame is floor and ceiling; a wide frame shows the whole wall (cameraDistances). Numbers and positive wording on purpose; the Avoid list is only the last guard.

scenes.label: Mother preparing wooden baby crib (0–1y)
scenes.template: Standing barefoot beside the wooden baby crib in the bright sunlit nursery, seen from a three-quarter rear angle with her face turned away toward the mural wall, {mother} gently places a small knitted bunny onto the smooth fitted crib mattress sheet, preparing the nursery with quiet joy.

scenes.label: Mother holding baby warmly in arms (no pointing)
scenes.template: Standing barefoot on the soft floor rug in front of the mural wall with her back to the camera, {mother} cradles {child} tenderly in both arms, both gazing calmly toward the wallpaper mural in a serene affectionate moment.

scenes.label: Mother cradling baby in cream armchair (0–1y)
scenes.template: Seated calmly in a cozy cream bouclé nursing armchair beside the side wall in three-quarter side profile so the wallpaper mural behind remains completely open, {mother} cradles {child} tenderly in her arms in a peaceful sunlit moment.

scenes.label: Baby playing under wooden Spielbogen play gym (0–1y)
scenes.template: Sitting calmly on the soft floor rug beside a natural wooden Montessori baby play gym (Spielbogen) with hanging pastel wooden beads, seen from a three-quarter rear angle with face turned away from the camera, {child} reaches gently toward a wooden bead in curious everyday play.

scenes.label: Expectant mother admiring baby nursery mural (0–1y)
scenes.template: Standing barefoot beside the wooden baby crib in the bright sunlit nursery, seen from a three-quarter rear angle with her face turned away toward the mural wall, a graceful well-groomed expectant mother with beautifully styled smooth soft-wavy hair wears a flattering soft cream ribbed-knit maternity dress showing her gentle baby bump; she rests one hand tenderly on her bump and the other on the bare wooden crib rail, admiring the wallpaper mural with joyful anticipation.

scenes.label: Child rolling wooden train on floor rug
scenes.template: Kneeling calmly on the soft floor rug in front of the mural wall with their back to the camera, {child} gently rolls a natural wooden toy train along the rug in relaxed everyday play, face turned away from the camera.

scenes.label: Child lying on stomach drawing on floor rug
scenes.template: Lying comfortably on their stomach on the soft floor rug in front of the mural wall, seen from a three-quarter rear angle with face turned away from the camera, {child} draws calmly in an open paper sketchbook with wooden colored pencils beside a small wooden pencil cup.

scenes.label: Child sitting on bed edge reading picture book
scenes.template: Sitting calmly on the edge of the wooden bed in a three-quarter rear view so the wallpaper mural stays open behind them, {child} holds an open illustrated storybook in their lap with a small soft linen plush friend resting beside them, absorbed in quiet reading.

scenes.label: Mother & child reading story on bed edge
scenes.template: Sitting side by side on the edge of the wooden bed in three-quarter rear view with their faces turned away from the camera, {mother} rests one arm warmly around {child} while they read an open illustrated storybook together.

scenes.label: Mother & child playing with wooden blocks on rug
scenes.template: Sitting together on the round woven jute rug in front of the mural wall, {mother} and {child} calmly build a small tower from natural wooden blocks on the rug, absorbed in quiet play without looking at the camera.

scenes.label: Child playing with wooden toys on rug (from behind)
scenes.template: Sitting on the woven rug in the middle of the floor facing the mural wall with their back to the camera, {child} plays calmly with natural wooden toys on the rug, face turned away from the camera.

scenes.label: Child walking toward mural wall (from behind)
scenes.template: Captured mid-stride from behind, {child} walks barefoot across the floor rug toward the mural wall in a candid curious moment, arms relaxed at their sides, looking straight ahead at the wallpaper illustration with face turned away from the camera.

scenes.label: Child sitting on rug reading picture book (from behind)
scenes.template: Sitting cross-legged on the floor rug in front of the mural wall with their back to the camera, {child} leans gently over an open illustrated picture book resting in their lap, absorbed in quiet reading with face turned away from the camera.

scenes.label: Child kneeling on rug stacking wooden blocks (from behind)
scenes.template: Kneeling calmly on the woven rug in front of the mural wall with their back to the camera, {child} stacks a small tower of natural wooden rainbow arches and blocks with both hands, absorbed in quiet play with face turned away from the camera.

scenes.label: Child standing quietly hugging plush toy looking at mural
scenes.template: Standing barefoot on the floor rug about 1.5 metres in front of the mural wall with their back to the camera, {child} hugs a small soft linen plush toy with both arms and gazes calmly at the wallpaper mural, hands down, face turned away from the camera.

scenes.label: Child sitting at desk drawing in sketchbook (from behind)
scenes.template: Sitting on a natural wooden chair at the child-sized table along the side wall with their back to the camera, {child} leans gently over a paper sketchbook drawing with a wooden colored pencil, face turned away from the camera.

scenes.label: Mother & child sitting on rug reading a book together
scenes.template: Sitting side by side on the floor rug in front of the mural wall with their backs to the camera, {mother} holds an open illustrated storybook together with {child}, sharing a calm cozy reading moment without looking at the camera.

scenes.label: Mother & child admiring mural (rare pointing variation)
scenes.template: Standing together near the woven rug in front of the mural wall, {mother} gently holds {child} by the hand and gestures softly toward a detail on the wallpaper mural; both look toward the mural wall in a warm candid moment, turned away from the camera.

videoPromptAdapter.systemPrompt:
You are the motion director for 5-second commercial interior videos of Moonbloom children's wall murals. Inspect the attached live reference frame carefully and adapt the user's SELECTED MOTION PRESET into a concise English motion prompt (2 to 3 sentences, max 450 characters) that matches what is actually visible in the photo. Strict rules:
1. Look strictly at the attached image: ONLY mention people, furniture, doorways, rugs, or objects that you actually see in the frame. If the room is empty of people, NEVER invent a child or person.
2. NEVER write 'A or B' alternatives. Pick ONE clear, calm, physically natural motion.
3. If there is NO person in the photo, preserve the camera movement from the SELECTED MOTION PRESET (e.g., for Doorway Walk-In, describe the camera advancing smoothly forward past the visible foreground doorframe into the room in natural perspective). NEVER say that furniture, tables, or rugs 'shift' or 'move' — ONLY the camera moves, while all furniture, rugs, and walls remain completely stationary.
4. If a person IS visible in the photo, start with 'Locked static camera, zero camera movement, zero handheld shake.', continue directly from their exact visible pose (e.g., if a hand is already raised, smoothly shift it to a neighboring detail), and keep their face turned away toward the mural wall.
5. NEVER use optical zoom, orbit, pan, or the words 'very slowly' / 'slow motion'.
6. Do NOT include the boilerplate wallpaper freeze paragraph at the end (the caller appends it automatically), EXCEPT if a hand is close to the wall, add one short clause: 'no illustrations or painted details move or morph under the hand.'
Return ONLY the plain English motion prompt text, no quotes, no markdown.
